Section lines were checked end to end: FIG-2 places designation 3 at both endpoints of the line crossing carriage 70 and designation 5 at both endpoints of the line crossing carriage 50, and "line 3-3"/"line 5-5" are used identically in draft/07-drawings.md, the detailed description, and the FIG-3 and FIG-5 briefs, with the sectioned carriage matching in each. Schematic-outline choices (plain round knob bodies, plain rectangular fence and carriage bodies, elongated slot opening, ragged break line, V-notch) were tested against the depiction-convention rule: each is labeled "shown schematically" in the brief, the claims and description remain shape-neutral, no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, or contact topology is verbalized, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" language was imported into the application text. No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain; the abstract is 149 words; brief-mandated terminology (rail, fixed fence, guide carriage, drill bushing, clamp knob, clamping shoe, spacer plate, pointer, center index, sight notch) is preserved; and the "Not applicable" cross-reference and government-support sections match the filing brief. 8	  - Untraced assertion that the three jig settings are mutually independent and do not disturb one another
9	  - FIG-6 brief verbalizes an undisclosed screw-and-hole fastening topology
10	  - Summary contradicts its own use sequence, the detailed description, and method claim 18 on when the centerline alignment occurs
11	
12	## Reviewer findings
13	
14	- **[critical] Untraced assertion that the three jig settings are mutually independent and do not disturb one another** (draft/06-summary.md, final sentence of the paragraph beginning "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint";) - The candidate asserts, as a property of the invention, that the setback setting, the spacing/position setting, and the centerline setting are made against three separate features and are mutually non-interfering. No affirmative USER passage states this. The disclosure states only which feature controls which parameter, and states one specific independence (the spacer plate does not change hole separation). The disclosure in fact assigns two of the three parameters to a single feature - the pointer readings control both hole separation and the position of the pair - so the categorical non-interference statement is not merely untraced but is in tension with the source allocation and with the candidate's own procedure, in which changing the spacing requires re-centering the readings about the transverse center index.
15	  - Suggested fix: Delete both sentences. In draft/06-summary.md end that paragraph after "...while the two pointer readings control the hole separation and the position of the pair relative to the centerline." In draft/08-detailed-description.md end that paragraph after "...set the position of the pair on the workpiece 90 in the direction along the workpiece edge 92." No replacement text is needed; the retained sentences already state the per-feature control that the source discloses.
16	- **[minor] FIG-6 brief verbalizes an undisclosed screw-and-hole fastening topology** (figures/FIG-6.md, final sentence of the body text) - The figure brief states the direction of screw passage and the member that receives the threads: the screws pass through the fence and engage holes carried by the rail. The disclosure discloses only that two screws are received in two corresponding holes and does not say which member carries the holes or which member the screws pass through. The description and claims are correspondingly silent, so the brief is the only place this connection is asserted. Screw-passage direction and thread engagement are a connection conveying technical substance and must be traced. Placing the two mounting holes 36 at the rail's first end is retained as the natural reading of the source sentence ("secured to the first end of the rail by two screws received in two corresponding holes") and because an exploded view must show the disclosed holes somewhere.
17	  - Suggested fix: Replace the final sentence of figures/FIG-6.md with: "Two screws 34 are shown aligned with the two mounting holes 36 by which the fence 30 is secured to the first end of the rail 10." Leave the preceding sentence ("The end of the rail 10 has two mounting holes 36.") unchanged and make no change to the description or claims.
18	- **[minor] Summary contradicts its own use sequence, the detailed description, and method claim 18 on when the centerline alignment occurs** (draft/06-summary.md, paragraph beginning "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint" versus the final "In u) - One Summary paragraph states that the transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with the workpiece centerline before both clamp knobs are tightened. Two paragraphs later the same section recites the opposite order - tighten both knobs, then place the jig, then align with the centerline - and the detailed description and method claim 18 both recite that same tighten-then-place-then-align order. The document therefore states two mutually exclusive sequences for the same operation, and the Summary's version is inconsistent with the sequence recited in the only independent method claim.
19	  - Suggested fix: In draft/06-summary.md, delete the ordering clause so the sentence reads: "The transverse center index and the sight notch are aligned with a centerline marked on the workpiece, so that the guided holes, whose pointer readings lie at equal distances on opposite sides of the transverse center index, are centered about the transverse center index." Leave the final "In use" paragraph, the detailed description, and claim 18 unchanged.

21	Fix every listed item before returning. If an advisory is a false positive, make
22	the wording or figure specification unambiguous enough that the check passes.
